html:
Escalating tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, marked by reports of tanker attacks and military posturing, coupled with intensified diplomatic efforts for a US-Iran deal, signal a critical juncture for global security and energy markets. This comes as the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange faces a record-breaking $6.3 billion cyber heist, further unsettling global finance.

US-Iran Tensions: The Strait of Hormuz is a focal point of escalating military tensions, with a ship reported on fire off Oman and multiple tankers struck by projectiles or explosives; Iran's IRGC Navy also reported stopping two tankers for unauthorized routes. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard additionally announced a third oil tanker explosion after colliding with a naval mine. The US is reportedly weighing new strikes on Iran post-midterms and has sent 10 military planes to Israel for a possible operation. Trump confirmed an outreach by Vance focusing on medical supplies, but a senior security source indicated Iran has not yet responded to Vance's letter. Amid this, Qatari mediators are in Tehran presenting a new deal to end the war. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated progress requires Iran's seven conditions to be met, and a Revolutionary Guards-affiliated outlet promoted calls for Iran to build an atomic bomb. Hegseth ousted an Army general as the US prepares for potential attacks on Iran, with a US senator calling Trump's plans to restart an Iran war "insane." The Pentagon estimates a war with Iran could exceed $47 billion.

Israel's Political Deadlock: Israel's consequential election has ended in a deadlock, with final results showing neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition secured a majority. Netanyahu's Likud party, which lost its majority, stands accused by the opposition of trying to 'delegitimise' the election, with claims of foreign interference and allegations that Arab-led parties "stole" the vote. A far-right Israeli minister is seeking the arrest of Arab party leaders. Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak suggested Netanyahu "lost dramatically" and that his rival Gadi Eisenkot should ally with Arab parties to form a government, although both Netanyahu and Eisenkot are claiming a mandate.

Global Economy & Cyber Security: US tech stocks have seen sharp falls, with shares in Intel continuing to decline and the tech-heavy Nasdaq opening at its lowest level in over two months, amid fears over AI costs. Concurrently, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, reported a record-breaking $6.3 billion hack, which blockchain intelligence firms link to North Korea; major crypto platforms froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen assets. Economists expect an upcoming GDP report to show economic growth, though they describe this growth as "fragile" ahead of Election Day. In Europe, ECB head Christine Lagarde is set to step down in February, before her term ends.

Great Power Dynamics: Japan and the US have agreed to establish a Japanese facility for joint missile production, an action by the allies who have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia. Meanwhile, China has elevated a military general to the Politburo and is seeking to strengthen party discipline, approximately a year before President Xi Jinping is expected to secure his fourth five-year term. Russia's independent media continues to face severe pressure, with Novaya Gazeta announcing its permanent closure next month, citing intolerable pressure as Russian society is "systematically crushed." Black Sea shipping faces growing threats, exemplified by a Greek container ship sinking after being struck by three drones, potentially of Russian origin, with reports also emerging of an Israeli cargo ship sinking off Bulgaria following a drone attack.

US Midterms & European Affairs: Pope Leo XIV made history as the first pontiff to vote in a US election, mailing in a ballot for the midterms from Chicago, where he was born. This comes as Trump has canceled two rallies, opting for telephone events across states before the elections, amid claims from Iran that it plans to disrupt the US midterms. In Europe, Spain is in a second day of mourning following a high-speed rail disaster that killed 69 people, with transport minister Óscar Puente refusing to resign amid calls to do so. France is bracing for a new wave of protests this weekend, with the interior minister warning of a "very high risk of public disorder" and deploying approximately 70,000 police officers.
